Hi Jordan / Priya —

Thanks again for the call today — great conversation and really appreciate the level of detail on your production constraints. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned before we put a draft SOW together: 

Recap (from discovery):
- Goal: Verify Redwood can meet Acme’s realtime classification latency (p95 < 120ms) while maintaining >=85% detection rate on your anomaly detection model.
- Data: You can provide a 10k event sample + 1k labeled anomalies for offline eval; production shadowing preferred for two critical routes (ingest and alerts).
- Constraints: Redaction + SOC2 evidence required; procurement needs a 30-day trial window.

Proposed POC plan (high level):
1) Offline eval: Redwood will run our evaluation harness on the 10k sample and the labeled set to measure accuracy and failure modes.
2) Online shadow (optional/parallel): 2-week shadow of production traffic for the two routes to measure latency/cost and live false-positive/negative rates.
3) Grading rubric: Combine automated metrics (precision/recall, latency p95, token cost) with a small human-review pass to validate edge cases.
4) Timeline: Kickoff next week, offline eval results in ~5 business days, shadowing to follow (2 weeks).

Attachments: Acme_POC_Eval_Plan_v0.1.xlsx (draft plan + data checklist)

Ask: Please confirm the following by EOD Monday so we can lock the timeline:
- Success criteria (do the metrics above map to what you need?)
- Which eval track do you want to prioritize first: offline eval only, or offline + online shadow in parallel?
- Who will own the labeled data delivery and annotation instructions on your side (name & email)?

I’ll draft the SOW once we have these answers. Thanks — looking forward to running this with you.

Best,

Jordan / Priya —

Echoing Marissa — happy to outline the technical eval approach. Attached is a starter rubric (eval_rubric_v1.csv) and a suggested timeline (poc_timeline.csv). High-level notes: 

Evaluation tracks (recommended):
A) Offline eval (required first step)
  - Redwood runs model inference on your 10k sample + 1k labeled anomalies.
  - Metrics we’ll report: precision, recall, F1; confusion breakdown by event type; semantic-similarity for ambiguous cases (embedding cosine).
  - Human annotation: we’ll sample 200 alerts for human review to estimate real-world pass rate.

B) Online shadow (recommended parallel if procurement allows)
  - 2-week shadow for ingest and alerts routes.
  - Metrics: latency p50/p95, error rates, token cost per 1k, throughput (req/s).
  - We’ll also capture model drift signals and surface top failure modes.

Grading rubric (proposal):
- Accuracy tiering: Pass if recall >= 85% AND human pass rate >= 90%.
- Performance tiering: Pass if latency p95 < 120ms AND error rate < 1%.
- Overall: All critical routes must meet both accuracy and performance for POC success.

Data & ownership:
- Acme provides labeled set + sample events (Jordan / Priya).
- Redwood will run offline harness, produce reports, and provide annotation guidelines for the human-review pass.

Next steps I can own technically: set up eval harness and provide test API keys for shadowing. If you confirm offline-only vs offline+shadow, I’ll schedule the run and drop the CSV rubric in the shared drive.

Attachments: eval_rubric_v1.csv, poc_timeline.csv

Thanks,
